## Workflow and responsibility

Cross Sections presents three hydraulic review regions: channel, left
descending-bank floodplain and right descending-bank floodplain. Polygon-derived
centerlines describe each region independently. They are
reviewable geometric direction proxies, not measured hydraulic flow paths.
The accepted MVP baseline in `dev/features/cross-section-layout.md` owns defaults,
requirements and scientific limits. All saved Streams and Reaches are eligible.
The owner accepts method-v10 channel polygon pruning and its defaults as the
preparation baseline. Further station/bank-order, endpoint-distribution and
bend-routing work must preserve that accepted recipe and its source evidence.

1. `mod_study_server()` mounts `cross_section_review_server()` with the linked
   Event selector and upstream revision signals. `load_flowline_points_review()`
   resolves exact saved Flowlines, Flowline Points and Hydro DEM inputs. A matching
   `flowline_points$loaded_inputs` value reuses the session's validated inputs;
   context/Event/revision changes force reopening. Opening is deferred until after
   the browser paints the status/progress indicator above the map. Cancellation
   tokens prevent hidden-tab or superseded callbacks from populating review.
   The status slot reserves its height. A CSS transition delays the synchronous
   busy fallback by 650 ms, so short worker polls do not flash another message or
   shift the map; explicit input-opening and worker phases remain immediate.
2. `cross_section_rem_queue()` queues saved Reaches from Flowline Points.
   `cross_section_rem_artifact()` calls `fluvgeo::detrend()` in a sequential
   background worker and publishes analytical/display REM GeoTIFFs, display
   limits and provenance. They persist across sessions with exact-input/recipe
   fingerprints and output hashes. Cross Sections reads those files immediately,
   preparing a missing Reach once when necessary. The inherited corridor can
   truncate evidence; the current metric project uses approximately 150 m.
3. The debounced `cross_section_layout_job()` worker reports inundation,
   centerline and deconfliction phases through its stdout pipe, with elapsed
   stage timings in its result. It calls `water_surface_extents()` with strictly ordered
   analyst levels. Original inundation retains holes; outer footprints fill
   holes without connecting disconnected parts.
4. `cross_section_regions()` partitions the outer footprint into three multipart
   parent regions with explicit component identities. Before partitioning, it
   derives a raw channel polygon centerline. `cross_section_mainstem_channel()`
   evaluates off-route lobes using boundary-distance discs along that centerline.
   A native depth screen rejects shallow chips. Single-attachment lobes qualify
   at 1 m depth and a depth/chord ratio of at least 0.5, with 0.5 m envelope
   padding. Tangent advance remains diagnostic so hooked arms can qualify.
   One overlay removes eligible lobes along the envelope. Validity, component
   count, the remaining original banks and reference route are protected. Raw channel,
   removed/candidate lobes and the reference centerline remain separate artifacts.
   The saved Flowline identifies the longitudinal skeleton route; the polygon
   channel centerline supplies the cleanup geometry. `centerline::cnt_skeleton()`
   and `cnt_path()` produce per-component Voronoi skeletons and longitudinal raw
   routes. A failed route whose anchors lie in disconnected skeleton fragments
   retries within the connected component with the greatest longitudinal span;
   diagnostics retain the fallback and span fraction, with no fragment joining.
   Douglas-Peucker/Chaikin proposals are retained only when simple and
   contained in their own component. Failures and rejected smoothing are explicit.
5. `cross_section_layout()` samples the saved measured Flowline, uses local
   tangents from the three polygon centerlines and constructs channel, LOB and
   ROB XS segments. An overbank uses the component touching its bank. A bank already on the
   outer boundary with no adjacent overbank is a zero-width floodplain side,
   distinct from missing/ambiguous direction evidence. A bank-to-centerline
   connector that leaves its polygon is replaced by the closest tested visible
   segment projection, preserving the source line and recording the adjustment.
   If the centerline is hidden around a bend, a cached constrained triangulation
   supplies a contained geodesic association, explicitly marked as inferred.
   A contained path to the outer boundary can seed an ordered target when no
   direct outward ray reaches it.
   Channel segments begin perpendicular to the local channel-centerline tangent.
   `cross_section_channel_deconflict()` jointly searches angular alternatives
   for contacting or bank-order-conflicted channel windows, including those with
   mapped overbanks, preserving full width, stations and
   strict bank rank/nonintersection. Cyclic boundary measures prune a bounded
   constraint search; actual bank arcs and GEOS contacts audit the result.
   A 2.5-degree grid, 30-degree search bound and separate provisional 15-degree
   review threshold retain larger departures as warnings. Window/node limits
   and unavailable solutions leave original flagged geometry. Width minimization
   is excluded. Selected banks then freeze. One-sided GEOS
   rays propose full-coverage floodplain endpoints within the angular bound;
   tentative alternatives reduce contacts and angular departure before rank
   assignment. `cross_section_boundary_chains()` extracts directed
   shared edges and whole-channel bank arcs. `cross_section_order_anchors()`
   assigns outer targets in Seq order; `cross_section_refine_targets()` can repair
   infeasible proposals inside their ordered neighbor interval before freezing them.
   `cross_section_ordered_routes()` builds complete nonintersecting floodplain
   routes to those fixed targets, treating other channels and accepted legs as
   barriers. A fixed target beyond the straight angular bound can try one
   genuine bend at half the endpoint distance, with its initial direction
   clamped to the bound; fixed endpoints, containment and contacts still govern.
   This proposal is only made when needed. Extra vertices are checked by default. When enabled, constrained
   triangulation/graph routing and visibility shortcuts can add multiple vertices
   away from centerlines. Unsupported routes and channel contacts stay explicit.
   Failed neighborhoods and geodesic-association neighborhoods can release their
   earlier reservations for group repair. Four deterministic priorities reuse a
   component mesh; complete-route count takes precedence over reducing interior
   crowding. Weighted mesh routes prefer room away from the boundary, with
   contained simplification/smoothing. Groups have at most 64 sections and 16
   exact polygon-route fallbacks. A repair replaces the current group only when
   its measured score improves, and banks/outer targets stay fixed.
   `cross_section_bend_plan()` then jointly tests targets and routes in crowded,
   incomplete or multi-bend families, including already complete legs. Overlapping
   neighborhoods form groups of at most 32 sections. Five boundary distributions
   and three routing priorities reuse a component mesh. Complete coverage precedes
   adaptive endpoint separation, then fewer unnecessary turns/backtracking.
   Replacements must complete the entire family, retain bank vertices and pass
   containment/nonintersection. Otherwise the incumbent remains. Final target
   measures and group-selection evidence are retained for save/reopen.
   Existing valid paths can guide contained deformation toward new targets.
   Mesh geometry, boundary clearance and point/triangle attachments are reused;
   each proposal still receives current obstacle and containment checks.
   Explicit left_bank_vertex/right_bank_vertex retain channel identity with two
   or more vertices. Endpoint banks permit channel-only or one-sided cross sections;
   absent/failed legs have no duplicate edges. section_parts describes geometry,
   while leg status and boundary gaps distinguish absence, failure and coverage.
   Adding a bend requires a constructed overbank. No leg is shortened. The backend routing helper is
   `cross_section_deconflict.R`, with ordering in `cross_section_order.R`;
   tests include multi-bend obstacles, fixed endpoints and a wide confluence.
6. Original polygons, components, skeletons and raw/smoothed centerlines are
   separately reviewable. Polygons/centerlines appear first; candidate cross sections
   and permanent Seq numbers appear by default. Advanced settings and manual
   correction are collapsed. Boundary spacing, Chaikin passes and local tangent
   distance are distinct parameters. Direction review points identify shortened
   tangent windows, raw-centerline use and unavailable direction evidence
   separately from incomplete geometry. A session cache reuses skeletons and
   centerlines when only cross-section spacing or tangent distance changes.
7. Map clicks move an armed vertex after transformation from display to analysis
   CRS. `cross_section_layout_review()` refreshes orientation, endpoint fields,
   all-pair touches/crossings, self-crossings, endpoint gaps and outside length.
   Channel-bank direction and the outer endpoint chord have separate flags:
   a winding overbank can reverse the chord without reversing the channel banks.
   The established combined `oriented` flag retains its original meaning.
   With boundary chains supplied it also refreshes actual bank/outer rank and
   channel departure from perpendicular without moving geometry. Generated
   target evidence remains distinct from later manual edits.
   Deletion resequences mutable `Seq` and preserves remaining local candidate IDs.
   `cross_section_vertex_labels()` identifies banks and optional bends. Add/Remove
   floodplain bend changes the selected side, keeping banks/endpoints fixed and
   refreshing bank indices. Manual additions start at the leg midpoint.
8. Save draft re-resolves upstream evidence and `study_cross_section_store()`
   publishes an immutable schema-9 / method-v11 GeoPackage revision with PENDING protection,
   exact input/output hashes, and RDS/JSON indexes. Reopening restores controls
   and corrections only for matching inputs and method. Incompatible drafts are
   never silently reused. Explicit lifecycle cleanup may retire obsolete automatic
   drafts after checking edits and retaining the accepted baseline.
   Changing controls can also reuse a saved draft for that exact settings set;
   readers verify the same lineage/output hashes before bypassing computation.

Raw input changes clear candidates before the 400 ms debounce expires. Workers
receive file paths and serializable inputs, validate their generation key, stop
before session cleanup and do not transfer raster external pointers. A failed
layout preserves valid inundation review. The analyst preview uses a fresh R
process and the isolated development backend library.

## Data objects and storage

| Object | Input/output | Representation and ownership |
|---|---|---|
| Flowline, Flowline Points, Hydro DEM | Exact saved Event/Reach inputs | Existing GeoPackage candidates and shared Stream GeoTIFF; resolved through the app store |
| Analytical/display REM | Persistent local preparation | Study-local cross-section-preparation/<input-recipe-hash>/rem.tif and display.tif; preparation.json/RDS retain source and output hashes; prepared by cross_section_rem_artifact, read by Cross Sections |
| Inundation and outer footprints | Selected levels and layout evidence | sf during review; saved source/outer polygon layers with draft |
| Three hydraulic regions | Channel, left and right floodplain parent polygons | `hydraulic_regions`, three MULTIPOLYGON rows including explicitly empty sides; `region_components` retains disconnected parts and local region_id |
| Skeletons and raw/smoothed centerlines | Independent polygon geometry and direction evidence | `centerline_skeleton`, `centerline_raw`, `centerline`; each row links to its source component and region role |
| Cross-section polylines and samples | Editable candidate geometry and local diagnostics | Standard `cross_section` and `side_support`; explicit bank indices, optional bend flags, leg status, generated channel deconfliction status, actual rotation and degree-valued search/review bounds, and tangent/raw-source flags; opaque local candidate IDs survive edits/reopen, Seq is mutable |
| Ordered edges and targets | Generated layout evidence | `boundary_chains` LINESTRINGs and `boundary_anchors` POINTs retain chain identity/role/orientation and candidate/Seq/side, planned boundary positions, status and explicit feature-CRS measure units. Whole-channel bank arcs check order across floodplain components. Actual section order flags are refreshed on edits/save. |
| Method and review evidence | Settings, source lineage, component failure/rejection and software | `layout_metadata`, `region_diagnostics`, provenance JSON and local reopening index |
| Mainstem channel preparation | Raw threshold polygon and its own polygon centerline | `channel_outer_raw`, `channel_reference_centerline`, `channel_branch_review`; prepared geometry is `channel_outer`; original inundation remains unchanged |

The owning schema is `dev/schemas/cross-section-drafts.md`. FGDB's naming contract
requires standard names with descriptive variables in tables. Historical fields
retain their types and meanings; exact compatibility details belong in the schema.
Region-specific
hydraulic calculations, governed identity/acceptance, additions, cross-Reach
collision management and legacy export remain open.

## Verification

Sibling `test_cross_section_regions.R`, `test_cross_section_layout.R` and
`test_cross_section_bend.R` cover
geometry, area/nonoverlap, side labels, containment, artifacts and cross sections.
`test-cross-section-review.R` and `test-cross-section-store.R` cover interaction,
invalidation, identity, metadata and GeoPackage reopening. The owner has accepted
the method-v10 channel-pruning recipe and defaults after review of the R2 arm
examples. Remaining layout refinements still require review of actual polygons,
centerlines and cross sections, especially narrow/disconnected components,
branching routes and end caps. The legacy toolbox Centerline
raster-thinning/PAEK code is inspected context and is not copied or invoked.

`test-cross-section-loading.R` covers prepaint progress, matching-input reuse,
cancelled loads, Reach selection and worker phase delivery. Performance evidence
and the repeatable audit entry point are in `dev/performance/cross-sections.md`.
Backend planar operations use CRS-free working copies only after checking the
projected source CRS and converting distances; returned geometry, units and
source artifacts retain the original CRS. Earlier accepted R1 drafts remain
unchanged; new layout methods create separate immutable revisions.
